title: Antibody-induced platelet activation - Potential impact on thromboembolic events in patients with antiphospholipid syndrome
summary:
Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a disorder of the immune system in which the blood has an increased tendency to form clots. As a result, thrombosis can occur, and women with APS experience miscarriages more often.
The cause is misdirected antibodies that mistakenly target the body’s own components involved in blood clotting. These antibodies affect, among other things, platelets, the blood vessel lining, and the immune system, making it easier for blood clots to develop.
Although patients receive medications that reduce blood clotting, thrombosis and miscarriages can still occur. It is thought that these antibodies change platelets in a way that makes them more easily activated. The exact mechanisms behind this are not yet fully understood.

interventions.name: Following consent during the routine blood draw: Collection of an additional serum tube (6 mL each)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- inpatient or outpatient patients with suspicion of APS
- age 18 years or older
Exclusion criteria:
no consent
